hero.kicker: La Calzada de Oropesa, Toledo · Opening spring 2027
hero.title: Return to what matters
hero.subtitle: An estate under construction inside a century-old olive grove, facing the Sierra de Gredos, two hours from Madrid.

thesis.title: An estate under construction
thesis.body: La Finca Oropesa doesn't open tomorrow. It is being built, stone by stone, among 1,200 olive trees — some of them a century old — planted long before us. When it opens, in spring 2027, there will be fifteen suites, a table cooking what the land gives, and a place built for doing nothing — and having that be enough.

facts.title: The place, in a few facts

items.label: The land
items.body: 1,200 olive trees, some of them a century old, in the first foothills of the Sierra de Gredos.

items.label: The Roman road
items.body: The village takes its name from the Roman road that linked Mérida to Toledo and ran through here.

items.label: An oil tradition
items.body: La Calzada de Oropesa once had five olive mills. The grove belongs to that history.

items.label: The castle nearby
items.body: A few kilometres away, the fortress of Oropesa became, in 1930, the first Parador in Spain set inside a historic monument.

items.label: The interior designer
items.body: The interiors will be designed by Tomás Alía, born in Lagartera, the next village over. Spain's National Interior Architecture Prize winner, he has always worked with the crafts of this land: Talavera ceramics, Lagartera embroidery, blown glass and wrought iron.

oliveraie.seoTitle: The Olive Grove — 1,200 olive trees in La Calzada de Oropesa | La Finca Oropesa
oliveraie.seoDescription: The land, the stone and the 1,200 olive trees of La Finca Oropesa, photographed before the estate's transformation in Castilla-La Mancha, Spain.
oliveraie.intro: Before it's a hotel, this place is a piece of land. 1,200 olive trees, some a century old, set in rows that follow the slope of the ground. These photographs show the finca as it was before construction began — the stone untouched, the trees unpruned for a season, the real silence of the Castilla-La Mancha countryside.

trees.title: 1,200 olive trees
trees.body: Every row tells a different story of the land: the chalky soil, the drought that toughens the roots, the short shade of silver leaves. None of this is built — it's inherited.

stone.title: Stone and the old buildings
stone.body: The estate's walls, the ground, the structure of the original buildings: the project builds on what already exists, rather than replacing it.

land.title: The land of Castilla-La Mancha
land.body: A flat horizon, the dry light of inland Spain, the scale of the Manchego landscape. It's this land that shapes everything else.

cta.title: See where this place is heading
cta.body: Discover the project being built here.

projet.seoTitle: The Project — 15 suites, spa and farm-to-table table | La Finca Oropesa
projet.seoDescription: Fifteen suites for two, a spa, a farm-to-table kitchen and wellness retreats: what will open at La Finca Oropesa in spring 2027.
projet.intro: Nothing below exists yet. It's being built. We describe it as it will be, not as it is today — no staged photos of what doesn't exist yet, because a serious project doesn't need to fake it.

suites.title: Fifteen suites
suites.body: Fifteen suites for two will sit at the heart of the estate, among the olive trees. The interiors will be designed by Tomás Alía, an interior architect born in Lagartera a few kilometres from here, who works with Talavera ceramics, Lagartera embroidery and wrought iron as raw material. A single suite type for now — differentiation will come later, as construction progresses.
suites.detailsNote: Size, amenities and views will be published before opening.

spa.title: The Spa
spa.body: A space built for real rest, with honest materials and silence as the main luxury.

table.title: The Table
table.body: A farm-to-table kitchen serving what the estate itself produces: oil, vegetables, whatever is in season.

retraites.title: The Retreats
retraites.body: Stays built to truly slow down, in a small group or alone. Here, we do nothing — and that's the whole point.
